title: ci-cd-rollback-breadcrumbs-local-debug-2025-11-14
content:
Context:
- Canary rollout for 2025.11.12 build (image: registry.redwood.internal/inference-api:2025.11.12-rc3, digest sha256:abcd1234efgh) started 2025-11-14 09:10 PST.
- Canary failed at ~3% traffic with increased 5xxs and degraded tail latency. Immediate rollback attempted but observed partial traffic still routed to canary instance for ~7 minutes. These are my raw breadcrumbs while debugging.

Timeline (quick):
- 09:10 canary deploy via pipeline (jenkins job: release/inference-api -> helm upgrade --install inference-api ./charts/inference-api --set image.tag=2025.11.12-rc3).
- 09:13 first 500 errors spike (slo alert).
- 09:15 manually triggered pipeline rollback to previous tag 2025.10.29-stable (jenkins rollback job).
- 09:15 helm rollback applied to release inference-api (helm rollback inference-api 39).
- 09:17 observed mixed pods: some still running 2025.11.12-rc3 image.
- 09:22 traffic finally stabilized on 2025.10.29-stable.

Commands I ran / outputs (copied):
- kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide | grep inference-api
  inference-api-rc3-5f6b8   1/1 Running   0     3m   10.10.8.21   ip-10-0-8-21
  inference-api-stable-9c4d1 1/1 Running   0     25m  10.10.7.12   ip-10-0-7-12

- kubectl describe deployment inference-api -n prod
  (noted strategy RollingUpdate, maxUnavailable=1, maxSurge=1)
  Events:
    Normal  SuccessfulCreate  2m    replicaset/inference-api-rc3-5f6b8 created
    Normal  ScalingReplicaSet 2m    Deployment scaled up replica set inference-api-rc3-5f6b8 to 1
    Normal  SuccessfulRollingUpdate 1m  Rolled out revision 40

- kubectl logs inference-api-rc3-5f6b8 -n prod --tail=200
  ERROR 2025-11-14T09:12:34Z [http] 500 internal server error: model load timeout after 30s (kv-cache: miss)
  WARN  2025-11-14T09:12:35Z [worker] slow token generation: 460ms
  ERROR 2025-11-14T09:12:40Z [http] 502 upstream read timeout

- curl -v "https://api.redwood.prod/inference/health" -H "Host: inference-api"
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK (for stable pods)
  HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error (for rc3 candidate behind lb)

Artifact/version notes:
- Candidate image: registry.redwood.internal/inference-api:2025.11.12-rc3 -> digest sha256:abcd1234efgh
- Stable image: registry.redwood.internal/inference-api:2025.10.29-stable -> digest sha256:wxyz9876mnop
- Jenkins job metadata: build 1542 -> tag 2025.11.12-rc3; promotion to canary only after smoke tests (smoke passed in staging but not in prod).
- Helm release revision bumped to 40 for rc3. Rollback to rev 39 succeeded but pods from rev40 lingered (race with service mesh?).

Hypotheses:
1) New image has model load behavior that occasionally times out under cold start; canary traffic (even 1-3%) caused backend to hit model load path and trigger 500s.
   - Evidence: logs show "model load timeout after 30s" and increased latency.
2) Pod lifecycle / readinessProbe misconfiguration: readiness probe might be passing before model fully ready, allowing LB to route requests to warm-up pods.
   - Check readiness probe config: initialDelaySeconds=5, periodSeconds=10 -> likely too aggressive for model load.
3) Service mesh (istio) sidecar causing delayed shutdown or traffic shadowing; rollback helm/rollingUpdate maxSurge/Unavailable small values caused mixed versions to get traffic during rollback.
   - Evidence: mixed pods observed after helm rollback. Need to check istio config (traffic shifting) and DestinationRule subsets.
4) Image tag immutability issue: pipeline used tag 2025.11.12-rc3 but did not pin digest in deployment; subsequent re-push? (low probability)

Immediate mitigation steps taken:
- Manual rollback via helm rollback -> started at 09:15.
- Increased canary safety: update pipeline to temporarily set canary traffic to 0 until we verify readiness probes. (follow-up PR created).
- Posted to #releases and #sre with incident breadcrumbs and linked RE-3219.

Next debugging steps / TODOs (ordered):
- Reproduce locally in staging with identical traffic profile (ramp traffic script). Try to reproduce "model load timeout" with same image digest.
  Commands:
    - k9s / kubectl port-forward svc/inference-api 8080:8080 -n staging
    - run load test: hey -n 1000 -c 20 http://localhost:8080/v1/generate?prompt=test
- Check readiness/liveness probe definitions in chart values:
    values: readinessProbe.initialDelaySeconds=5 -> increase to 60, readinessProbe.failureThreshold=3
- Confirm image digest pinned in chart/templates/deployment.yaml (image: {{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}@{{ .Values.image.digest }})
- Inspect istio virtualservice/destinationrule for canary routing rules (maybe using header-based routing); run: kubectl get virtualservice -n prod inference-api -o yaml
- Request sidecar logs for one rc3 pod: kubectl logs inference-api-rc3-5f6b8 -c istio-proxy -n prod --tail=200

Notes to self / lessons learned:
- Always pin digest for production canaries to avoid tag drift.
- Readiness probe must reflect worst-case model load time (start with 60s for large models).
- Consider adding a "warmup" job during deploy that prepopulates KV cache / triggers model load before pod enters ready state.
- Increase canary gating: require 5 minutes of successful low-eps traffic or a healthcheck that exercises model endpoints.

Links / refs:
- RE-3219 (incident ticket)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-engineering/pull/452 (pipeline change: pin digest & adjust canary percentage)

Open questions / things to ask SRE:
- Did Istio/Envoy report any aborted connections or 503s at the mesh level around 09:12? (ask @Priya)
- Was there any recent change to kube node autoscaling or pod eviction policies that could cause pods to get killed and redeployed during rollout?

Quick reproduction checklist (for pairing with Sam):
- Pull candidate digest locally, deploy to staging with identical helm values (including replica counts, probes).
- Run short synthetic tests hitting cold-start path.
- If reproduces, collect pprof/heap+cpu for worker process to see if OOM or heavy GC correlating with timeouts.

Scratch/notes end. Will iterate after pairing session 2025-11-18.
